rows.title: A new experiment in remote work … from the inside
rows.standfirst: When people in Maine prisons started getting laptops to use in their cells for online classes and homework, it sparked this new idea. Could they have laptops in their cells to work remotely for real outside world jobs, too??? And get real outside world wages?

rows.title: What to do if your flight gets canceled because of the government shutdown
rows.standfirst: The FAA is cutting 10% of air traffic at 40 of the nation's busiest airports, canceling hundreds of flights and creating uncertainty for many more passengers. Here's what to do if you're one of them.

rows.title: OpenAI's new web browser has ChatGPT baked in. That's raising some privacy questions
rows.standfirst: The Atlas browser can act as your "agent" online, doing tasks like shopping or booking tickets. But that gives it access to a lot of personal information.

rows.title: What's happening with furniture prices? A tale of $399 couches and tariffs
rows.standfirst: Competition, whether from overseas rivals or second-hand goods, has kept the price of furniture relatively low. New tariffs may boost U.S. makers — and raise prices.

rows.title: Is the job market getting worse? As the shutdown continues, this is what we know
rows.standfirst: For the second month in a row, a government report on employment and unemployment has been delayed by the federal shutdown. That leaves analysts looking for other signs to gauge the job market.

rows.title: Can air traffic controllers keep calm and carry on — without pay?
rows.standfirst: There’s one job that gets all the attention during a government shutdown: air traffic controllers. Today on the show, we spotlight why this job has taken on outsize political influence and one controller’s experience during the longest shutdown on record. rows.title: Boeing won't face criminal charge over 737 Max crashes that killed hundreds of people
rows.standfirst: As part of a deal to dismiss the case, Boeing agreed to pay or invest an additional $1.1 billion in fines, compensation for the crash victims' families, and internal safety and quality measures.

rows.title: Tesla shareholders approve Elon Musk's trillion-dollar pay package
rows.standfirst: Tesla shareholders have approved a pay package for Elon Musk that could allow him to earn an unprecedented one trillion dollars' worth of stock.

rows.title: Wall Street reckons with life under Zohran Mamdani
rows.standfirst: New York City's CEOs and other billionaires spent more than $40 million trying to defeat the mayor-elect. Now they have to live with him.

rows.title: ICE is sending a chill through the construction industry
rows.standfirst: The construction industry, where more than a quarter of workers are foreign-born, has long struggled to find enough workers. Now, industry officials say Trump's immigration crackdown is making it worse.

rows.title: Is your electric bill going up? AI is partly to blame
rows.standfirst: Across the country, demand for electricity is on the rise — and so is the price of electric power.

rows.title: Your credit history could be costing you more to drive
rows.standfirst: Auto insurance companies often use credit history as a factor in setting premiums

rows.title: This indicator hasn’t flashed this red since the dot-com bubble
rows.standfirst: The “Shiller PE Ratio” is at its highest level since November of 1999. That was at the peak of the online gold rush right before the dot com bubble burst in 2000. Today on the show, we learn what the Shiller PE Ratio is, how it works and whether we should be worried that it’s relatively high right now.

rows.title: Supreme Court put Trump tariffs on a high-fire grill, in bipartisan scrutiny
rows.standfirst: At issue is whether the president can bypass Congress and impose tariffs by citing national security.

rows.title: Prosecutors seize yachts, luxury cars from man accused of running Cambodia cyberscams
rows.standfirst: Prosecutors in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore seized hundreds of millions of dollars in assets belonging to a Cambodian businessman whom the U.S. accuses of heading a global scam syndicate.

rows.title: Scott Bessent's $20 billion dollar gamble on Argentina
rows.standfirst: Last month, during the longest government shutdown in U.S. history, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the United States had offered to functionally loan Argentina $20 billion. Despite the sums involved, this bailout required no authorization from Congress, because of the loan’s source: an obscure pool of money called the Exchange Stabilization Fund. The ESF is essentially the Treasury Department’s private slush fund.

rows.title: Trump scraps tariffs on beef, coffee, tropical fruit in a push to lower prices
rows.standfirst: President Trump announced the removal of U.S. tariffs on beef, coffee, tropical fruits and other commodities amid pressure to address high consumer prices.

rows.title: Better late than never: The delayed September jobs report will be out next week
rows.standfirst: The Bureau of Labor Statistics says it will report on September's job gains and unemployment rate next week. That's the first of many overdue economic reports held up by the government shutdown.

rows.title: Alaska station that covered devastating storm cuts jobs
rows.standfirst: A public TV and radio station in Western Alaska serves dozens of villages damaged by Typhoon Halong. But with federal funding eliminated, KYUK makes severe cuts to its staff and news department.

rows.title: Judge says he'll approve opioid settlement with OxyContin maker Purdue and Sackler family
rows.standfirst: A federal bankruptcy court judge said he will approve OxyContin-maker Purdue Pharma's latest deal to settle thousands of lawsuits over the toll of opioids that includes some money for thousands of victims of the epidemic.

rows.title: She criticized President Trump during the shutdown. Now she's been put on leave
rows.standfirst: Jenna Norton has spoken critically about the Trump administration's funding cuts and mass firings at the National Institutes of Health. At the end of the shutdown, she says she was put on leave.

rows.title: BBC apologizes for edit of Trump speech but says it won't provide legal compensation
rows.standfirst: The BBC has apologized to President Trump for the way it edited his Jan. 6, 2021, speech but says it won't pay compensation. Trump has threatened a $1 billion lawsuit against the British broadcaster.

rows.title: Economic promises helped Trump get elected. Now he has an affordability problem
rows.standfirst: Americans are feeling the strain of high prices, even as President Trump tries to tout "record highs" in the stock market.

rows.title: 50-year mortgages, falling real wages, and doing your rideshare due diligence
rows.standfirst: It’s … Indicators of the Week! We look at some of the most fascinating economic numbers from the news and bring them to you.

rows.title: Clothing rentals on the rise as shoppers and retailers brace for tariffs impact
rows.standfirst: More consumers are quitting buying clothes in favor of renting, to cut cost as rising inflation and tariffs pushing apparel prices higher.

rows.title: Where the US got $20B to bail out Argentina
rows.standfirst: The U.S. is committed to bailing out Argentina to the tune of $20 billion using a little known mechanism called the Exchange Stabilization Fund. On today’s show, what is this fund, why was it created and does Argentina have any hope of paying it back? Related episodes:

rows.title: 3 questions about Trump's 50-year mortgage plan
rows.standfirst: Experts in the mortgage industry are skeptical. Buyers would pay less each month, but would end up paying more over time. Here's what to know about the proposed 50-year mortgages.

rows.title: Buy now, pay dearly? (update)
rows.standfirst: (Note: A version of this episode originally ran in 2022.)

rows.title: Google launches a lawsuit targeting text message scammers
rows.standfirst: Ever gotten a text saying you forgot to pay a nonexistent road toll or need to pick up a mystery package? Google's going after the scammers behind those messages.

rows.title: Trump's backup options for tariffs
rows.standfirst: The U.S. Supreme Court may soon rule on President Trump’s favorite tariff law. It could render them moot, but that doesn’t mean the end of tariffs. On today’s show, we explain the president’s back-up options for imposing tariffs.

rows.title: The Consumer Sentiment vs. Consumer Spending Puzzle
rows.standfirst: Wherever consumer sentiment goes, consumer spending usually goes too. They’re like buddies that do everything together. Consumer sentiment wants a hair cut, its buddy consumer spending does too.But lately, these friends are drifting apart.While consumer sentiment about the economy is down … spending remains strong. And not just that… Interest rates are still high, inflation is growing, tariffs have made the prices of goods go up. And yet, consumer spending looks good. What gives?Today - a consumer spending mystery. Is the economy actually healthy? Or is something distorting our view of the economy? rows.title: The female crash test dummy has been a long time coming — but she isn't here yet
rows.standfirst: After years of limbo, the U.S. government has given the green light to a crash test dummy based on the female body. But will it be used right away? Not so fast.

rows.title: Rare earths: Federal backing and tech advances aim to help the U.S. catch up to China
rows.standfirst: Rare earths aren't all that rare. The real choke point is in processing and refining them, where China enjoys market dominance.

rows.title: Pay transparency. The WhatsApp and Instagram decision. Our beef with screwworms.
rows.standfirst: It’s … Indicators of the Week! Our weekly look at some of the most fascinating economic numbers from the news.

rows.title: Recalled baby formula linked to a botulism outbreak may still be in some stores
rows.standfirst: A botulism outbreak that has sickened more than two dozen babies in 15 states has been linked to ByHeart formula sold nationwide. Here's what to know about it.

rows.title: Overdue jobs report shows employers added 119,000 jobs in September
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers added 119,000 jobs in September, while the unemployment rate inched up to 4.4%. The report, which was delayed by the government shutdown, may hint at the pace of hiring and firing.

rows.title: College 'sticker prices' have risen dramatically. Here's why
rows.standfirst: It's no secret that going to college can be very expensive, with tuition costs rising faster than financial aid. But what's causing that price tag to rise so quickly?

rows.title: Trump administration seeks to roll back protections for imperiled species and habitat
rows.standfirst: The Interior Department proposed reviving a suite of changes to Endangered Species Act regulations first made during the Republican's first term. Those changes were reversed under former President Biden.

rows.title: How to avoid scammers after a natural disaster
rows.standfirst: When people lose their homes to wildfire, hurricanes or flooding, they're eager to rebuild. But scammers are also ready to take advantage. On today’s show, the lucrative business of contractor fraud and advice on how to avoid them. Related episodes:

rows.title: How a small Chicago nonprofit is resisting Trump's war on DEI
rows.standfirst: Since 1981, Chicago Women in Trades has worked to promote equity by getting more women into the construction trades. Now the nonprofit faces a different challenge: Trump's efforts to erase DEI.

rows.title: Days of our Tariffs
rows.standfirst: Tariffs. They’ve been announced, unannounced, re-announced, raised and lowered. It’s an on-going saga with billions at stake!

rows.title: Looking for love in the auto supply chain
rows.standfirst: Foreign automakers already have huge assembly plants in the U.S., but lots of parts and materials come from overseas.

rows.title: Judge sides with Meta in antitrust trial, will not spin off WhatsApp and Instagram
rows.standfirst: A federal judge ruled against the Federal Trade Commission's antitrust suit alleging that Meta had stifled competition by buying up its rivals.

rows.title: Farewell, fair penny. You are finished, but never forgotten
rows.standfirst: This tiny disc of zinc with just a smidge of copper has played an outsized role in our national (and international) discourse. The U.S. Mint ended production of the one-cent coin last week.

rows.title: Is a 50-year mortgage really that much crazier than a 30-year one?
rows.standfirst: Last week, the internet piled on President Trump's proposal for a 50-year mortgage. But maybe it's not as crazy as it sounds.

rows.title: Airbus calls for 'immediate' software upgrade to A320 aircraft
rows.standfirst: A320 planes are flown by a number of domestic and international airlines, and the required software update could lead to "operational disruptions to passengers and customers," according to Airbus.

rows.title: Capitalism (Taylor's Version) (25-minute Podcast Version)
rows.standfirst: Taylor Swift reaches new heights with her latest album, which is both divisive and record-breaking. And it’s fueled by an elaborate series of business choices that propel profits but also chart numbers. rows.title: This expert watches shoppers like a hawk. Here's her holiday forecast
rows.standfirst: Retail expert Katie Thomas scours her local shopping mall in Pittsburgh to divine what Americans' shopping habits reveal about the economy and the nation's future.

rows.title: Saving lives with fewer dollars
rows.standfirst: Givewell is a nonprofit organization that gives money to “save or improve the most lives per dollar.” Part of their whole thing is a rigorous research process with copious and specific datapoints. So, in the chaotic wake of USAID’s gutting, they scrambled to figure out if they could fund the kind of projects USAID used to.

rows.title: AI is transforming crime, too
rows.standfirst: By the midpoint of 2025, the U.S. was on track to set a new yearly record in the number of reported data breaches.That’s according to data compiled by the Identity Theft Resource Center.One reason is the proliferation of artificial intelligence, which has made the work of criminal hackers easier, cheaper and scalable.What does that mean for the rest of us?

rows.title: 4 marketing tricks to not fall for this holiday season
rows.standfirst: Retailers use marketing techniques to get you to spend more, like creating a false sense of urgency or creating artificial discounts. Outsmart the gimmicks with these tips.

rows.title: How to watch the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
rows.standfirst: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is back this year and promises to be bigger than ever. Here's a preview of what to expect and how to watch.

rows.title: The U.S. produces a lot of food waste. This place wants to address it
rows.standfirst: Even amid rising grocery prices and increased sensitivity to environmental issues, Americans still trash once-edible food at alarming rates.

rows.title: Moochers, monopolists and market-based poverty help
rows.standfirst: Public sector economics is a fundamental piece of the discipline. So we wanted to give our hosts an opportunity to put their knowledge to the test in a game we’re calling Indicator Quizbowl. Today on the show, Wailin and Darian go head to head to see who the bigger public policy nerd is. Related episodes:

rows.title: New limits for rent algorithm that prosecutors say let landlords drive up prices
rows.standfirst: Landlords could no longer rely on rent-pricing software to quietly track each other's moves and push rents higher using confidential data, under a settlement between RealPage Inc. and federal prosecutors.

rows.title: 8 economic insights we're grateful for
rows.standfirst: For this Thanksgiving, Planet Money and The Indicator staffers offer economic insights they're grateful for.

rows.title: We're shopping our feelings this Black Friday. Here are 3 things to know
rows.standfirst: Signs are pointing to deeper discounts this Black Friday, as stores try to coax anxious shoppers into splurging.

rows.title: Who's financing Meta's massive AI data center?
rows.standfirst: In a rural pocket of northeastern Louisiana, Meta is building a $30 billion data center called Hyperion. But it’s not being completely financed with Meta’s own money. Today on the show, the opaque system of AI data center financing and why it’s fueling fears of a bubble.

rows.title: Portland Trail Blazers coach pleads not guilty in rigged poker games case
rows.standfirst: Hall of Famer Chauncey Billups has pleaded not guilty to charges he profited from rigged poker games involving several Mafia figures and another former NBA player.

rows.title: Give thanks for the discounts: The feast will cost a little less this year
rows.standfirst: Shoppers can be thankful for discounts on turkey and stuffing this year. While overall grocery prices are up, this year's Thanksgiving meal should cost a bit less than last year's.
